thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Ends 3-day Losing Streak As Earnings Lift Stocks

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Ends 3-day Losing Streak As Earnings Lift Stocks
text:
By Anora M. Gaudiano, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Google parent Alphabet surges after beating profit estimates
U.S. stocks ended mostly higher on Tuesday, powered by a number of positive earnings, including much stronger-than-expected results from the parent company of Google.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 197.65 points, or 0.8%, to finish at 25,241.94, as three of its components reported earnings, ending a three-day losing streak.
The S&P 500 index gained 13.42 points, or 0.5%, to close at 2,820.40, with nine of its 11 main sectors closing higher. Telecoms, materials and energy sectors lead the gains, up more than 1%.
The Nasdaq Composite Index , which hit a record earlier, pulled back from highs to end marginally lower--off 1.11 points--at 7,840.77.
Read:Tech rally is putting stocks mere points away from ending a lengthy bearish streak (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tech-rally-is-putting-stocks-mere-points-away-from-ending-a-lengthy-bearish-streak-2018-07-24)
What's driving the markets?
Earnings news dominated the action on Tuesday, as the busiest week of the season continues. Shares of Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL)(GOOGL) jumped 3.9% a day after it reported results that topped expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/alphabet-stock-soars-to-potential-record-highs-as-google-earnings-smash-expectations-2018-07-23). The stock closed at a record after its biggest one-day percentage jump since October 2017.
Read:Google is a great investor, and Alphabet earnings are showing the results (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/google-is-a-great-investor-and-alphabet-earnings-are-showing-the-results-2018-07-23)
Google parent Alphabet is one of the so-called FAANG group of stocks, which also includes Facebook Inc. (FB), Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Apple Inc. (AAPL) and Netflix Inc. (NFLX), that have fueled the overall market's advance over the past several years. The results could provide comfort that the quintet of huge internet and technology stocks still have room to run. Facebook and Amazon are scheduled to report later this week. Facebook (FB) shares rose 1.8% on Tuesday, hitting a record of their own.
Read:Earnings Watch: 35% of S&P 500 companies set to report in a crazy week (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/earnings-watch-35-of-sp-500-companies-set-to-report-in-a-crazy-week-2018-07-23)
Also read:Facebook earnings: Amid controversy, finances appear bulletproof (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-earnings-amid-controversy-finances-appear-bulletproof-2018-07-23)
The second-quarter earnings season has largely been strong. According to data from Charles Schwab, with 22% of the S&P 500 having reported thus far, 91% of companies have topped earnings expectations, while 75% have come in ahead of revenue forecasts.
Issues surrounding trade remained in focus, however, particularly after President Donald Trump tweeted that tariffs are "the greatest." Escalating tensions between the U.S. and its major trading partners have been a major concern of investors of late, amid fears that the situation could evolve into a full-blown trade war.
(https://twitter.com/realDonaldTrump/status/1021719098265362432)
See:The 'significant damage' a U.S.-China trade war could do to the global economy--in one chart (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-significant-damage-a-us-china-trade-war-could-do-to-the-global-economy-in-one-chart-2018-07-23)
In the latest economic data, the manufacturing and service sides of the U.S. economy showed steady and rapid growth in July (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-economy-growing-steadily-in-july-markit-pmis-show-2018-07-24), according to a preliminary or "flash" reading by IHS Markit.
Read:This selloff in U.S. government debt will prove short-lived, Morgan Stanley says (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fade-this-selloff-in-us-treasurys-morgan-stanley-says-2018-07-23)
What are market analysts saying?
"Markets are grinding higher but headline risks, such as tariffs, are tamping down enthusiasm among investors," said Karyn Cavanaugh, senior market strategist at Voya Financial.
"This quarter is shaping up to be another barnburner of a quarter. We're seeing a very large percentage of companies beating expectations and we don't think we've seen a peak yet," said Janet Johnston, portfolio manager at TrimTabs Asset Management, who singled out Alphabet as a company that had "a blowout quarter."
She added, "trade remains the biggest risk out there, and if the issue continues to grow it'll become a worry, but at this point there's still time to work out the issues until tariffs that have been announced get implemented."
What stocks are in focus?
Biogen Inc.(BIIB) jumped 4.1% after the company posted adjusted second-quarter earnings that easily beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/biogen-shares-surge-42-on-q2-profit-revenue-beats-2018-07-24), along with revenue that handily topped forecasts. Eli Lilly & Co.(LLY) advanced 5% after the company's second-quarter results came in well above expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/eli-lillys-stock-jumps-after-earnings-beat-potential-ipo-of-elanco-animal-health-2018-07-24).
3M Co.(MMM) rose 0.9% after the Dow conglomerate reported better-than-expected earnings and revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/3m-co-shares-rise-23-on-q2-beats-guidance-raise-2018-07-24) and raised its outlook.
United Technologies Inc.(UTX) gained 3.8% after it reported second-quarter earnings and sales that topped analyst forecasts. It also raised its outlook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/united-technologies-stock-rallies-after-earnings-and-revenue-beat-raised-outlook-2018-07-24). The stock provided one of the biggest boosts to the Dow.
Verizon Communications Inc. (VZ) rose 1.5% after the Dow component topped analyst forecasts on both earnings and revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/verizon-shares-rise-3-after-company-beats-2q-earnings-and-revenue-expectations-2018-07-24).
Lockheed Martin Corp. (LMT) rose 1.3% after the defense contractor reported second-quarter earnings and sales that came in ahead of expectations. It also raised its outlook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/lockheed-martins-stock-jumps-after-profit-and-revenue-beats-raised-guidance-ranges-2018-07-24).
Harley-Davidson Inc. (HOG) surged 7.7%. The motorcycle company reported adjusted second-quarter earnings that beat expectations, along with stronger-than-expected revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/harley-davidson-tops-profit-and-revenue-estimates-2018-07-24).
JetBlue Airways Corp.(JBLU) reported adjusted second-quarter earnings that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/jetblue-tops-adjusted-profit-estimates-for-second-quarter-2018-07-24). However, the stock tumbled 10.2%.
Whirlpool Corp. (WHR) plummeted 15% after the appliance maker surprised by swinging to a quarterly loss (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/whirlpool-shares-tank-on-surprise-quarterly-loss-lower-sales-2018-07-23) with lower sales and a downbeat outlook on revenue.
Read:IPO market braces for 11 deals, including a $1.5 billion deal from China's Pinduoduo (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ipo-market-braces-for-11-deals-including-a-15-billion-deal-from-chinas-pinduoduo-2018-07-23)
Shares of FCB Financial Holdings Inc.(FCB) dropped 12% after the Florida-based community bank announced a deal to be bought (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fcb-financials-stock-drops-after-synovus-buyout-deal-at-a-discount-2018-07-24), at a discount to Monday's closing price, by Synovus Financial Corp. (SNV). Shares of Synovus lost 8.7%.
What are other markets doing?
European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-step-higher-getting-a-boost-from-bank-shares-2018-07-24) moved higher, led by gains for UBS and other banks, while Asian stocks pushed higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-bounce-back-led-by-gains-in-china-2018-07-23), rebounding from losses a day earlier.
The U.S. dollar held steady, with the ICE Dollar Index off less than 0.1% to 94.620. Crude oil (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-tick-higher-as-us-iran-tensions-down-played-for-now-2018-07-24) rose 63 cents, or 0.9%, to $68.52 a barrel, while gold prices (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-sees-lackluster-action-as-a-rise-in-global-stocks-caps-benefit-of-weaker-buck-2018-07-24) settled slightly lower at $1,225.50 an ounce.
The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note fell 2 basis points to 2.95%.
--Barbara Kollmeyer contributed to this report
